articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.

articles.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
articles.summary: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.

articles.title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
articles.summary: Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: New rewritable displays can show an image for months without power
articles.summary: Researchers from the ARC Center of Excellence for Transformative Meta-Optical Systems (TMOS) are the first to report a reflective display based on antimony selenide that can hold an image for months without being powered.

articles.title: Trade war over green tech has no winners
articles.summary: In a study published in the journal Energy Research & Social Science, Dr. Lukas Hermwille and three co-authors outline the consequences of a trade war over environmental technologies. Such a trade war would significantly drive up the global costs of combating climate change—with Europe being hit hardest. There is reason to fear that this would make achieving the global climate targets difficult, if not impossible.

articles.title: Chatbots may leapfrog web search in sub-Saharan Africa
articles.summary: AI chatbots may leapfrog web search in sub-Saharan Africa, according to a study of teachers in Sierra Leone. Mobile phones are common in Africa, but only 37% of the population uses the internet. Among those internet users, social networking apps are much more commonly used than search engines, in part because search brings up large foreign websites that gobble up costly data to download.

articles.title: Smart homes of the future must put people before technology
articles.summary: Homes that automatically adjust their temperature, manage electricity use and monitor residents' well-being could transform everyday living in the future, but smarter technology does not necessarily mean better homes.

articles.title: New laser welding process joins aluminum castings with fewer pores and less spatter
articles.summary: Laser welding can now join cast aluminum directly to cast aluminum. Producing high-quality joints between aluminum die-cast components has long been a major challenge. Process-related pores and gas inclusions in the material can open during conventional laser beam welding. The released gases cause pores in the weld and sometimes violent melt ejections, compromising joint quality.

articles.title: UK 'Grand Theft Auto VI' hacker gets 7-year sentence
articles.summary: A U.K. court sentenced a British hacker to seven years in jail Monday for a series of cyberattacks, including leaking footage from "Grand Theft Auto VI" years before the blockbuster game's release.

articles.title: Harnessing glacial lakes for hydropower
articles.summary: As mountain glaciers retreat in the face of a warming climate, glacial lakes are expanding, increasing the risk of glacial lake outburst flood events that cause damage and destruction to communities downstream. However, harnessing the power of this excess water could both provide a renewable energy source for these communities and help reduce flood risks.

articles.title: Technology for 'printing' steel could help extend the life of aging bridges and buildings
articles.summary: The U.K. has an enormous amount of steel in service across critical infrastructure. Yet every day, millions of people cross bridges without giving much thought to the structures beneath their feet.

articles.title: New benchmark could help AI keep up with current events
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is struggling to keep up with the world. When queried about recent events, chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude often rely on the same sources people have used for years to find information online.

articles.title: Rwanda and Papua New Guinea had big energy access plans: Study compares what happened
articles.summary: In both Rwanda and Papua New Guinea, only about 10% of the population had electricity in the early 2000s. Both countries have rural populations that are difficult to reach with national electricity grids. Both partly privatized their electricity sectors and set ambitious targets for increased energy access.
